text:
marta: Heads up — after yesterday's rollout (r/merge 4921) we're seeing OOM spikes on longctx instances. Started ~08:30 UTC. P95 mem climbs and then kernel panics on a bunch of hosts. :frowning_face:

junaid: seen it too, started when kernel-router change landed + the new autobatch boundary heuristic. same hosts are the longctx machines.

devon: confirmed on my repro; kv cache free fragments spike during prefix-heavy requests. reproduction steps are tiny: send 2 requests with seqlen 8 then one with seqlen 4096 -> mem goes from 60% -> 98% and then oom.

samir: can you paste the logs/oom trace? sounds like fragmentation or slab churn. could be the kernel selection path picking an mmap-based allocator in the hotpath.

marta: paste of follower logs:
```
[2026-03-18T08:31:12Z] runtime: allocate slab 64k failed: out_of_memory
[2026-03-18T08:31:12Z] kvcache: slab_frag_pct=78.4 seq_len=4096 inflight=3 kernel_route=kernel-x86-mmap
[2026-03-18T08:31:12Z] runtime: stack dump ...
```

marta: also attaching quick flame (small sample) — the allocator hot functions spike after the kernel hop.

infra-bot: CI perf alert: https://ci.redwood.local/job/merge/4921 -> longctx memory regression + perf-test throughput -12% :eyes:

junaid: hmm the kernel-router change introduced a fallback that prefers kernel-x86-mmap for seqlen > 2048 when batching is low. Maybe that path has a different slab compaction heuristic.

devon: i bisected locally — if i disable the kernel-router patch (commit 3f7a8) the repro doesn't OOM. With it -> OOMs. so it's likely the selection policy not the allocator itself.

samir: suspect interaction: selection to mmap kernel + new batch boundary causes many small allocations to coexist with large kv pages -> fragmentation. Need to check eviction scoring change in the same deploy.

marta: right — we also shipped a tiny eviction tweak (pr #5082) that increments lifetime score more aggressively. Alone it looked fine in unit perf but combined with kernel hop it's bad.

junaid: plan: revert kernel-router selection (fast) and run canary. then reproduce with both changes to confirm the combinatorial regression.

devon: i'll open a revert PR for the router with a clear note. quick rollback should restore stability.

deploy-bot: Rollback PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/5091 — rolling back kernel-router selection change. initiating canary rollback to 4 instances in us-west-2.

marta: while rolling back, can we collect a detailed heap profile from a failing host? need to see fragmentation map + per-slab occupancy. cc @samir

samir: on it. grabbing jeprof and kvcache maps. also will run synthetic workload that spikes seqlen mix (8/256/4096) to stress the boundary.

infra-bot: FYI test matrix: bench/longctx-heavy shows mem 2.3x when both patches present vs baseline. filmstrip attached to CI ticket.

junaid: after rollback we should consider a safer selection rule: prefer non-mmap kernels for sessions with hot prefixes or where kvcache occupancy > 60%. add a gate in kernel-router to consult kvcache telemetry.

marta: agreed. also add a short-circuit: if slab_frag_pct > 60 then do not switch kernels mid-request.

devon: triage notes for postmortem: root cause = interaction between kernel selection heuristic + eviction score tweak -> pathological slab fragmentation for mixed seqlen workloads -> OOM. immediate mitigation = rollback. medium-term = telemetry-gated kernel routing + unit test for mixed seqlen cache stress.

samir: uploaded heap profile: https://artifacts.redwood.local/heapprofiles/1719004321/heap-1.heapprof (contains per-slab occupancy and free-runlists)

marta: thanks. once canary finishes we'll monitor p95 mem and CPU. leaving the rollback as priority until we have a safe routing rule implemented. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary rollback completed on 4/4 hosts at 08:47 UTC. No new OOMs observed in 15m window.

marta: closing thread for now, moving to follow-up doc for the longer fix. i'll create the postmortem draft and link to bisect notes.

devon: adding unit test ticket: https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/7812 -> mixed-seqlen eviction/regression test.

junaid: thanks all. follow-up: include a perf gate in CI that runs mixed seqlen sampler to catch this earlier.

marta: noted. good catch everyone. :heart:
